Fallout 76 — Um jogo bom prejudicado por uma experiência ruim

Fallout 76 é, sem dúvida, um jogo interessante. O universo é cativante, a narrativa tem potencial e existe muito conteúdo capaz de prender o jogador. Porém, minha experiência particular foi extremamente frustrante por um motivo que considero grave: a navegação e a acessibilidade dos menus são péssimas.

O jogo é excessivamente burocrático.

A construção do CAMP é um dos maiores exemplos. Em praticamente qualquer outro jogo de sobrevivência, construir uma pequena base com quatro ou seis blocos é algo rápido e intuitivo. No Fallout 76, uma tarefa simples pode consumir 10, 15 ou até 20 minutos, não porque a construção seja complexa, mas porque o sistema é contraintuitivo, possui diversos menus e exige uma navegação desnecessariamente complicada.

A localização das peças, a seleção dos objetos e todo o processo de construção parecem ter sido projetados para dificultar algo que deveria ser simples e prazeroso.
.

E o problema não termina aí.

O Pip-Boy e o inventário também são extremamente difíceis de navegar. Quando você acumula muitos itens, encontrar aquilo que realmente precisa pode se tornar uma tarefa cansativa e estressante. Em determinadas situações, existem itens que deveriam ser consumíveis, mas que não podem ser utilizados da maneira esperada, seja por limitações do sistema ou até mesmo por problemas que parecem bugs.

O mesmo problema aparece no acesso às lojas, ao passe de temporada e a outras funções do jogo. Os menus não são facilmente acessíveis e não existe uma navegação realmente fluida entre os diferentes sistemas.

É impressionante que um jogo com tantos recursos tenha uma interface que, em vez de facilitar a vida do jogador, parece constantemente colocar obstáculos no caminho dele.

E isso tem uma consequência muito séria: a desistência acontece antes de o jogador desenvolver uma paixão pelo jogo.

Antes de você ter tempo para se apaixonar pelo universo, descobrir tu…

citations.review_text:
Pros:
-The only new fallout content we have in 2026
-A few pretty decent story ideas
-Fun and interesting locations
-Some pretty cool weapons
-Atmosphere and music are pretty solid
-You can become a ghoul
-You can drop nukes
-The community is very nice and helpful, especially to new players
Cons
-Severely over monetized, providing both cosmetic and actual in game benefits
-Online only unless you pay a subscription
-Most quests can be summed up as "go here and kill this thing/bring this item back"
-Severe levels of "your princess is in another castle"
-subpar performance and stutters despite middling visuals
-Several main and side quests are broken and have been broken for several months
-Mid-late game is a terribly slow grind
-Writing is often underwhelming, cliche, and simplistic
-Little to no meaningful choices or consequences
-Builds are not permanent, you can change them at any time
-Severely limited item storage unless you pay a subscription

Summary: This game has some really good aspects that I like. However, these are severely disrupted by several changes made in order to make it online and reach a wider audience. The game is the definition of breadth not depth. On top of that, the monetization of this game is egregious and that alone is enough for me to encourage you not to support it. If you enjoy a casual and mindless MMO grind with fallout branding slapped on top of it, then you'll like this game. If you're expecting an actual RPG or a fallout experience, then you are better off looking elsewhere.

Got the game for 10$ during a sale and its been a blast. Some quests are a bit glitchy and feel like fetch quests but the overall game is amazing. Many people say you can play this game without interacting with the multiplayer content but from my experience this is not true as you will eventually need to do multiplayer events to obtain better loot. Doing bounty hunts and clearing out infestations with the community is a blast and building a camp is awesome as you can place it practically anywhere. The game also contains many different build types and approaches to combat. You can be a ghoul gunslinger like the show or a walking tank with heavy artillery depending on how you build your character, If you can get this game on discount for 10-20$ I'd definitely recommend buying it as you can sink many hours into it and always have something new to do.

citations.review_text:
[h3]Fallout 76[/h3]

[b]The Short Answer:[/b] 
An amazing co-op wasteland experience to play with friends, but heavy jank, botched execution on key features, and legacy issues make it a game I can only barely recommend.

[b]Recommended For:[/b]
[list]
[*]Groups of friends looking for a casual open-world survival RPG to explore together.
[*]Fallout fans who enjoy camp building, looting, and cooperative event farming.
[/list]

[b]The Good:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Co-Op Fun:[/b] Wandering Appalachia, tackling events, and building camps alongside friends is easily the best part of the game.
[*][b]World Design & Map:[/b] The Appalachian setting offers great location variety, distinct enemy types, and solid environmental storytelling.
[/list]

[b]The Bad:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Botched Features & Junk Content:[/b] Failed ideas like the abandoned Nuclear Winter PvP mode show how poorly executed certain systems were.
[*][b]Persistent Engine Jank:[/b] Server lag, quest bugs, frame hitches, and classic Bethesda stability issues still drag down the experience.
[/list]

[b]Steam Deck Performance:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Settings/FPS:[/b] Playable at 30–45 FPS on Low/Medium settings, but suffers from frame drops during busy public events and in heavy camp areas.
[*][b]Controls & UI:[/b] Controller support works well for combat and inventory, though navigating menus on the smaller screen can feel slightly crowded.
[*][b]Battery Life:[/b] Always-online nature and processing load result in heavy battery drain (~1.5 to 2 hours max).
[/list]

[b]Final Score:[/b] 5.5 / 10
😅👍🤷‍♂️

DO NOT BUY THIS GAME AT FULL PRICE, BUY IT ON A DEEP SALE

The game is not worth buying for $40 in my opinion, so I highly recommend waiting for a sale. It drops to $8–$10 pretty often throughout the year and was even $3.99 during the December sale, so definitely save your money.

The game is fun overall, and as someone who has played Fallout since the third game came out, I enjoyed this one too. The public events spread across the map are a blast to do with other players, and the base building is a major highlight. It is cool to customize your own space where your imagination and available items are the only limits. Having player-run shops to trade with others is also a neat feature that adds to the experience, especially since you can buy old seasonal items you might have missed.

It is completely enjoyable without a paid subscription, too. The various missions and stories are accessible without it. Out of all my playtime, I only had Fallout 1st for a single month just to get the ranger armor; aside from that, my time has been without it. Keep in mind you do have some limitations when you don't have it but its still fully playable. 

However, the game has its share of bugs. I have run into a fair number of them throughout my playtime, so if you expect a perfect game, keep on moving. You will still hit frequent server disconnects, choppy framerate drops during big public events, hit registration issues where your shots don't register, and laggy menus. There is even a weird glitch where your character loads in frozen in place—which just happened to me toward the end of May—so it is definitely still a problem. The developers should work on addressing these ongoing issues, but for me, the flaws aren't enough to stop me from playing.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that enemy difficulty relies heavily on massive hit point pools and bullet-sponge scaling rather than deep mechanics.

citations.review_text:
Game has a lot of locations and quests that are fun to explore, but the game has issues. Microtransactions aside, most of the game's difficulty directly comes from higher difficulty = higher hit points, not better mechanics. Some of the enemies in the game are so goofily tanky and bullet spongy that the only way to kill them is the abuse every mechanic available to stack damage. 

If you're a single player, good luck. This game is often designed around a team, and if you want to try something no one else on the server is interested in, you're out of luck, and can try the event/raid/quest, but you're going to have an uphill struggle unless you want to min-max like crazy, if the event is doable solo.

TLDR; If you like fallout and exploring, great! If you don't have a group of friends who love this game, and aren't autistically interested in how the game mechanics work under the hood, you're going to hate parts of this game.

The  seasons keep getting worse and worse. Full of camp titles, prefixes and suffixes or just reskined toilet and bathtubs. The infestations are extremely lackluster. The bosses either die in under 1 minute or are bullet sponges ( I prefer they are hardened to kill so you can at least get a shot or two In before they die.)
I think the real kicker for me this season (and ultimately why I’m not going to recommend the game) is the $30 deathclaw pet dlc. 
You can’t get it in their atoms shop, it’s not in the score board. It’s $30 dlc. They do something like this each season but this one really got to me. It seems….greedy. I sincerely hope no one buys the deathclaw pet bundle. Spend you money on something else. Grounded 2 or subnautica 2 are currently $30 and are great EA games that keep getting updates. 
I canceled my fallout first and fully uninstalled the game. It’s a shame too, I enjoy the base building and the cryptids in the game but it just seems like the company is getting greedier. Giving less and charging wayyyy more. 
If I feel like they changed I will edit my review but until then I don’t recommend getting into this money trap, FOMO game.
